title: Make Boss easy to open on iPhone
goal: Give the two Boss users a frictionless way to start reviewing work from their iPhones.
done: Both users can open the Safari Home Screen app and find their own first decision card.
plan: Check the first run on an iPhone and simplify the steps the users actually need.
next: Read the answer to choose the first-run path, then validate it on an iPhone and note any friction.
card: ### What should we test first on iPhone?
Options: Home Screen install | Safari tab
Recommend: Home Screen install, so Boss is always one tap away
- Home Screen install matches daily use, but it adds a short setup step.
- A Safari tab is faster to start, but it is easier to lose.

title: Resume Boss work after a decision
goal: Make sure a Boss decision gets back to the worker building Boss.
done: A worker claims an answered Boss issue, reads the answer, and records the next action in its log.
plan: Try the pickup mechanism on the Boss queue before enabling a standing schedule.
next: Read the answer. Run one scoped pickup for Run on demand, or set up a scoped schedule for Check on a schedule. Record the first pickup.
card: ### How should the first Boss worker resume after an answer?
Options: Run on demand | Check on a schedule
Recommend: Run on demand, so the first pickup is easy to watch
- On demand needs one manual start after you answer.
- A schedule runs unattended, but an answer may wait until the next check.

title: Review how Boss shows decision priorities
goal: Make it clear which Boss decision needs attention first without opening every issue.
done: A phone reviewer can distinguish urgent, routine, and unlabelled decisions at a glance.
plan: Check the ranking on a narrow screen with mixed priorities.
next: Read the answer about priority text, then check how it fits on a phone with long task titles.
card: ### What names should Boss show for decision priorities?
Options: P1, P2, P3 | Urgent, Normal, Low
Recommend: P1, P2, P3, to match the labels on the issues
- Numbers are compact and match GitHub.
- Words are easier for newcomers but take more space.

title: Check Boss queue and task history
goal: Keep existing Boss flows working as the team starts using it to build Boss.
done: Refresh, workstream filters, Move, completed history, and search pass a phone-sized smoke test.
plan: Run the existing browser checks and add a regression only if a flow is uncovered.
next: Run the existing PWA browser checks and note any gap in the issue log.
